To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transgenic perennial rygrass events with altered carbohydrate composition and increased in vivo digestibility have been developed and that these events are now being used for further breeding.
transgenic perennial rygrass events with altered in vitro dry matter digestibility and fructan concentrations have the potential not onlu to increase animal production but also pasture intake.

the transgenic events have a significant (P <0.05) increase in fructan concentration in leaf blades in the T0 events and an increase in metabolizable energy of 1.7 MJ ME·kg dry matter−1 in the spring and summer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transgenic perennial forage grass with altered fructosyl transferase (FTase) activity and altered fructan content and composition.
the development of a molecular breeding programme to develop transgenic perennial ryegress events with altered fractan biosynthesis through expression of fructotransferases.
the development of transgenic forage grasses for the improvement of the nutritive value and digestibility for the animal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

transgenic perennial rygrasses with increased fructan concentrations and decreased NDF concentrations in the leaves have the potential to improve the nutritive value and animal production of the grass.
the molecular breeding of transgenic plants with altered fructosyl transferase activities is a successful approach to improve nutritive value of perennial ryegrass forage.

the expression of the fructosyl transferase genes in the transgenic perennial rygrasses has the potential to increase the nutritive value of the grasses in spring and summer, which would have a beneficial effect on animal production and pasture intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transgenic perennial rygrass plants have increased fructan concentrations and improved digestibility and metabolisable energy in spring and summer, but have no effect on digestibility and metabolizable energy in winter and autumn.

the transgenic perennial rygrass plants were shown not to have any negative effects on plant development and that there was a significant increase in water-solduble carbohydrate concentration and in vitro dry matter digestibility concentration of the leaf blade of transgenic T0 perennial ryegrass.
the transgenic events with altered frucosyltransferase activity have the potential to improve forage quality of perennial ryegrass and thus to increase the productivity of dairy and beef herds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of molecular breeding technologies in perennial ryegrass has the potential to increase the nutritional value of this important temperate grass.
transgenic perennial rygrasses can be produced and that they are able to express the transgenes over several generations, which is a prerequisite for their use in breeding programmes.
it is possible to alter fructan biosynthetic pathways in transgenic perennial rygrass, and that this can lead to changes in nutritive values and animal production.
